How sourdough rises

This report, written for Ore's tests in the shape ChatGPT's page copies, opens with the main claim: a starter's wild yeast and bacteria raise a loaf more slowly than baker's yeast, and the wait is where the flavour comes from.example.org+1

What the starter does

Yeast numbers grow along a curve until the flour runs out. A simple model writes the population after ttt hours as follows.

N=e−t/SN = N_0 e^{rt}R

  • Yeast: makes the gas that lifts the dough.

  • Lactic bacteria: make the acid that gives the sour taste.

Proof times that work

Kitchen atBulk proof
20 °CSix to eight hours
26 °CFour to five hours

A feeding calculator

def feed(starter):

The closing advice is plain: feed the starter at the same time each day, and bake when it has doubled.
